title: Fine logarithmic structures and labelled etale descent data
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme and $(U_a\to T)_{a\in I}$ a family of objects of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Use the monoid sheaves, structural maps, geometric stalks and chart predicate of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. A log structure $M$ is fine if at every geometric point it has an etale neighbourhood with a chart $P\to M$ where $P$ is finitely generated and its canonical map to its group completion is injective. For a prelog structure $A$ on $U_a$, and $f:V\to U_a$ in the small etale site of $T$, its localized sections and structural map are those of $A$ on $V\to U_a$; restriction along $W\to V$ is the original restriction. Localization is the slice-site restriction of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. A fine-log descent datum consists of fine log structures $M_a$ on $U_a$ and monoid isomorphisms $\phi_{ab,V,f,g}:M_a(V\xrightarrow f U_a)\simeq M_b(V\xrightarrow g U_b)$ for every etale $V\to T$ with lifts $f,g$. They commute with all restrictions and structural maps, obey $\phi_{aa,V,f,f}=1$, and satisfy $\phi_{bc,V,g,h}\phi_{ab,V,f,g}=\phi_{ac,V,f,h}$ for every triple of lifts. By the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product], these are exactly isomorphisms on double overlaps with the diagonal and triple-overlap cocycle conditions. A gluing of the datum by a log structure $M$ on $T$ consists of natural, structure-preserving monoid isomorphisms $e_{a,V,f}:M(V)\simeq M_a(V\xrightarrow f U_a)$ with $\phi_{ab,V,f,g}e_{a,V,f}=e_{b,V,g}$. For arbitrary monoid sheaves $A,B$ on $T$ with structural maps $\alpha,\beta$, a homomorphism (respectively isomorphism) over the structure sheaf is a natural monoid homomorphism (respectively isomorphism) $h$ satisfying $\beta h=\alpha$. A localized homomorphism over $U_a$ is the analogous morphism of the slice restrictions $A|_{U_a}\to B|_{U_a}$ with the same structure-map equation; no log condition is imposed on $A$ or $B$.
